items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: And so I thought well of course I have to leave some room to blow. And I mean there are stories about Mozart taking requests from audiences in concerts.

ctx.x: And that’s like a real advantage, right? Like you’ve got this sort of built-in new sound every once in a while because as far as I know no one else is doing this exact thing.

Not really. It’s a funny thing how that concerto came about but I wrote it as a commission for an orchestra in Chicago. And I never studied composition, I never studied orchestration. And I just had to do it myself. And so I did. I wrote it out in pencil and then I gave it to a copyist and they made parts and made a score and everything. And the first time I performed it I was kind of terrified in certain ways because I also left room for myself to improvise in each movement. The first movement has a big cadenza,…
